# Full Significance record draft

Fill in what you know. Write “unknown”, “not checked”, or “not applicable”
instead of guessing. Repeat evidence, source, contributor, and task entries
as needed. Maintainers turn this intake draft into a version-bound record;
submitting it does not automatically publish a page or establish correctness.

This issue and its comments are public. Include only public sources and
information you want published. Do not paste private correspondence, email
addresses, credentials, or unpublished work without permission.

## 1. Page and contributors
- Proposed page title:
- New record, or existing record URL to update:
- Your public name/handle and public profile link (optional):
- Your role (author / reader / editor / other):
- Authors and other contributors, with public identity links:
- Author involvement (requested this page / opted in / public-source editorial draft / not contacted / unknown):
- Public source for author participation or permission, if available:

Ordinary claims by individual living authors require an author request or
explicit opt-in before publication. A reader's request is not author consent.
Maintainers handle private permission separately; do not post its contents here.

## 2. Claim and scope
- Exact mathematical claim or theorem statement:
- Where the source states it (URL, theorem/section, page, and short quotation):
- Hypotheses, definitions, and conventions needed to read it:
- What this page covers:
- Related stronger statements or cases this page does not cover:
- Original problem, conjecture, or tracker link and problem number (if any):

## 3. Exact source version
- Paper/manuscript title and authors:
- Public manuscript/PDF URL:
- Publication or upload date, if known:
- Version identifier (arXiv version, DOI, release tag, or pinned commit):
- Code/formalization repository and exact commit, if any:
- Supplementary files or datasets and their versioned URLs:
- Earlier/later versions or other Significance records this replaces or builds on:

Maintainers retrieve and hash the exact files. You do not need to compute a
SHA-256 or assign a record ID yourself.

## 4. Reader summary
- What the authors claim, in plain language:
- What has actually been checked, by whom, and how:
- What has not been checked or remains unresolved:

## 5. Evidence and review (repeat for each item)
- Kind (source inspection / external formal artifact / informal review / mathematical assessment / other):
- What was done or reported:
- Public name/handle of the person or organization reporting it:
- Date and exact source version examined:
- Scope (specific theorem, passage, code declaration, or computation):
- Source/receipt URL and precise location:
- Findings, limitations, and unresolved questions:
- Author response and its public source, if any:

Link existing build logs, receipts, commands, environment details, and output
when available. Do not invent a successful rerun or execution receipt.
An author's formalization and an independent reproduction are separate items.
If none exist, say so; maintainers can record their own source inspection.

## 6. Reported AI use
- Systems/models and versions, if disclosed:
- Roles (idea generation, proof drafting, coding, formalization, editing, etc.):
- What humans did and what AI did, to the extent known:
- Public disclosure source and location, or “unknown”:

## 7. Reviewer map and formalization handoff
- Main deduction or route through the argument:
- Most delicate steps, with page/theorem/code locations:
- Background/prerequisites and suggested reading order:
- Formal statement and its source/commit, if one exists:
- Differences or open correspondence questions between the paper and formal statement:
- Extra assumptions, axioms, trust boundaries, or computational dependencies, if known:

## 8. Explanation and context
- Plain-language explanation of the idea:
- Mathematical context, earlier work, and related records:
- Why this result may matter, and who makes that assessment:
- Sources and exact locations supporting each explanation or importance claim:

Attribute opinions and interpretations. Separate an author's claim of
importance from a contributor's assessment.

## 9. Focused help wanted (repeat for each task)
- A concrete question or bounded task:
- Why it would help:
- Exact passage, statement, file, or declaration to start with:
- Prerequisites and expected deliverable:
- Estimated effort, if known, and who estimates it:
- Public discussion link, if any:
- Participation status (open / someone working on it / completed / unknown):
- Person working on it and dated scoped report, if already available:

## 10. Attribution and careful wording
For each supplied finding, explanation, interpretation, or assessment:
- Who is asserting it, and on what date:
- Basis (author's own account / source quotation / contributor's inference):
- Supporting public URL and page, section, line, or short quotation:
- Suggested wording and qualifications needed to avoid overstating the evidence:
- Competing accounts or conflicts of interest, if relevant:

## 11. Corrections and changes (for an existing page)
- Section or entry to change:
- Current wording and proposed replacement:
- Supporting source and version:
- What changed since the earlier record, and when:

## 12. Publication notes
- Missing information or questions for maintainers:
- Which supplied material you are willing to have attributed to you publicly:
- Relevant public author approval, or permission still to be obtained:

Maintainers review attribution and source versions, apply the publication
rules, prepare the record YAML and history, run validation, and propose a
pull request. Unknown review results remain unknown. No field in this draft
certifies the mathematics or substitutes for independent review.
